verses.zh: 论海旁旷野的默示：有仇敌从旷野，从可怕之地而来，好像南方的旋风，猛然扫过。
verses.en: This is an oracle[NOTE:1] about the wilderness by the Sea:[NOTE:2] Like strong winds blowing in the south,[NOTE:3] one invades from the wilderness,from a land that is feared.
notes: See note at Isa 13:1.

The phrase is quite cryptic, at least to the modern reader. Verse 9 seems to indicate that this message pertains to Babylon. Southern Mesopotamia was known as the Sealand in ancient times because of its proximity to the Persian Gulf. Perhaps the reference to Babylon as a “wilderness” foreshadows the destruction that would overtake the city, making it like an uninhabited wilderness.
Or “in the Negev” (NASB).
verses.commentary:
21:1 "oracle" This NOUN (BDB 672) is litrally "burden" (cf. Exod. 23:5). See
full note at isa. 13:1.

▣ "the wilderness of the sea" This may be an attempt to translate

- the Assyrian name for Babylon (Mat + Amil, cf. JB footnote)

- the Akkadian title "Land of the Sea" (Mat tam-tim, i.e. southern Babylon), but it was
now destroyed, so "land" changed to "wilderness"

- The Peshitta and JPSOA translate it as "the desert of the sea," probably referring to the marshy area near
the mouths of the Tigris and Euphrates Rivers.

- TEV just has "Babylon."

The term "wilderness" (BDB 184) denotes large pieces of uninhabited land.

21:1-2a Isaiah tries to express his deep emotion when he receives this oracle.

- like a windstorm in the Negev, Isa. 21:1

- from a wilderness, Isa. 21:1

- from a terrifying (BDB 431, KB 432, Niphal PARTICIPLE) land, Isa. 21:1

- harsh (BDB 904) vision, Isa. 21:2a

21:2b This describes the invasion of old Babylon by Assyria in 703 B.C. (cf. Isa. 21:9; see
IVP Bible Background Commentary, OT, p. 611).

- the treacherous one still deals treacherously, play on BDB 93, KB 108, two Qal
ACTIVE PARTICIPLES, 24:16; 33:1; Jer. 3:20; 5:11 (it is possible
that the NIV and REB translations "traitor," or NRSV, "betrayer" historically fits
Merodach-baladan, the king of old Babylon, better)

- the destroyer still destroys, play on BDB 994, KB 1418, two Qal
ACTIVE PARTICIPLES, 16:4; 33:1; Jer. 6:26

21:2c God commands two northern Mesopotamian powers to attack old Babylon.

- "Go up" (BDB 748, KB 828, Qal IMPERATIVE) Elam (BDB 743). This is
surprising since initially Elam helped old Babylon to hold off Assyrian domination.

- "Lay siege" (BDB 848, KB 1015, Qal IMPERATIVE) Media (BDB 552). This
was another ethnic group in the northern Euphrates area.

It is possible that these are war cries of those in the anti-Assyrian coalition (i.e. Elam, Media,
so says the Jewish commentator Ibn Ezra). This would make more sense if Babylon of Isaiah's day is being
addressed.

21:2d "I have made an end of all the groaning she has caused" The MT has "all the sighing
I bring to an end" (BDB 991, KB 1407, Hiphil PERFECT). The JPSOA footnote suggests
an emendation, "Put an end to all her merrymaking."

The phrase, "she has caused," NASB, is not in the MT. If it is to be assumed, it must be stated
that this line of poetry fits Neo-Babylon better. This later empire had a much larger area of influence (i.e.
Nebuchadnezzar II, cf. Daniel 4).

Again, some (including me) see this last line as a statement from the old Babylonian king
(Merodach-baladan) or his deities (Marduk) directed to a "to-be-defeated" Assyria/Nineveh. There are so
many speakers in this chapter it is hard to know the intended speaker (the prophet, YHWH, Babylonian king,
several watchmen, unknown voices).

verses.zh: 令人凄惨的异象已默示于我。诡诈的行诡诈，毁灭的行毁灭。以拦哪，你要上去！米底亚啊，你要围困！主说：我使一切叹息止住。
verses.en: I have received a distressing message:[NOTE:1] “The deceiver deceives,the destroyer destroys.Attack, you Elamites!Lay siege, you Medes!I will put an end to all the groaning.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “a severe revelation has been related to me.”
This is often interpreted to mean “all the groaning” that Babylon has caused others.

verses.zh: 所以，我满腰疼痛；痛苦将我抓住，好像产难的妇人一样。我疼痛甚至不能听；我惊惶甚至不能看。
verses.en: For this reason my stomach churns;[NOTE:1] cramps overwhelm melike the contractions of a woman in labor.I am disturbed[NOTE:2] by what I hear,horrified by what I see.
notes: Heb “my waist is filled with shaking [or “anguish”].”
Or perhaps, “bent over [in pain]”; cf. NRSV “I am bowed down.”
verses.commentary:
21:3-4 The prophet describes the effect the message had on him personally. Daniel also experienced
physical distress at YHWH's revelations (cf. Dan. 7:15,28; 8:27; 10:16-17).

- loins are full of anguish

- pains have seized me like the pains of a woman in labor, cf. Isa. 13:8; 26:17

- I am so bewildered (i.e. bent over) I cannot hear, cf. Isa. 19:14 (i.e. an idiom of drunkenness)

- so terrified I cannot see

- my mind reels

- horror overwhelms me

- the twilight I longed for has been turned for me into trembling ("twilight" possibly Babylon's
defeat meant a stronger, more expansionistic Assyria)

All of these VERBS are PERFECTS, which
denote a complete situation. Why was he so distressed? There is no one to stop Assyria now!
She is coming!

21:3

NASB
"bewildered"

NKJV, NJB
"distressed"

NRSV
"bowed down"

REB
"distraught"

JPSOA
"to anguished"

Peshitta
"dismayed"

The VERB (BDB 730, KB 796, Niphal PERFECT)
basically means "to bend" or "to twist." It is regularly used of human sin as a perversion of God's truth/law (Isa. 21:3;
Prov. 12:8; Lam. 3:9).

For a brief word study, see Millard Erickson, Christian Theology, 2nd ed., pp. 592-593.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SIN IN THE OT, A. #2

verses.zh: 我心慌张，惊恐威吓我。我所羡慕的黄昏，变为我的战兢。
verses.en: My heart palpitates,[NOTE:1] I shake in fear;[NOTE:2] the twilight I desiredhas brought me terror.
notes: Heb “wanders”; perhaps here, “is confused.”
Heb “shuddering terrifies me.”
verses.commentary:
21:4 This verse expands on Isa. 21:2a ("a harsh vision"). It describes Isaiah's reaction to this oracle.

- my mind reels, BDB 1073, KB 1766, Qal PERFECT

- horror overwhelms me, BDB 129, KB 147, Piel PERFECT

- the twilight I long for has been turned for me into trembling, BDB 962, KB 1321,
Qal PERFECT

The question is, "Why was Isaiah so upset at the fall of old Babylon?" Possibly because of

- the terrible violence involved

- Babylon kept Assyria in balance. Now Assyria was free to expand region-wide (see Exposition Bible
Commentary, vol. 6, p. 134).

verses.zh: 他们摆设筵席，派人守望，又吃，又喝。首领啊，你们起来，用油抹盾牌。
verses.en: Arrange the table,lay out[NOTE:1] the carpet,eat and drink![NOTE:2] Get up, you officers,smear oil on the shields![NOTE:3]
notes: The precise meaning of the verb in this line is debated. Some prefer to derive the form from the homonymic צָפֹה (tsafoh, “keep watch”) and translate “post a guard” (cf. KJV “watch in the watchtower”; ASV “set the watch”).

The verbal forms in the first three lines are infinitives absolute, which are functioning here as finite verbs. It is uncertain if the forms should have an imperatival or indicative/descriptive force here.
Smearing the shields with oil would make them more flexible and effective in battle. See J. N. Oswalt, Isaiah (NICOT), 1:394.
verses.commentary:
21:5 This verse has a series of four Qal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTES
(functioning as IMPERATIVES) and then two Qal IMPERATIVE.

- set the table

- spread the rugs (see note following)

- eat

- drink

This would denote a lavish meal. Some commentators see this as referring to Daniel 5. If so,
then this chapter refers to Neo-Babylon of a later period (i.e. Nebuchadnezzar II).

In the midst of the party a messenger arrives and calls them to military preparations
("captains," BDB 978).

- rise up, BDB 877, KB 1086, Qal IMPERATIVE

- oil the shields, BDB 602, KB 643, Qal IMPERATIVE. The ancient
warriors covered their shields with leather so that flaming arrows would penetrate the soft
leather and be extinguished, cf. 2 Sam. 1:21.

▣

NASB, NJB
"spread out the cloth"

NKJV, Peshitta
"set a watchman in the tower"

NRSV, TEV, REB
"spread the rugs"

JB
"cover it with cloth"

LXX
"prepare the table"

JPSOA
"set the table"

This phrase is made up of a NOUN and a very
similar VERBAL root.

- NOUN, צפית
(BDB 860 II) found only here, some scholars see it as "carpet," others as "watchman"
(BDB 859, מצפה)

- VERBAL, צפה (BDB 860 II,
INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE), meaning "lay out" or "lay over"

Since people of the ANE ate sitting on the floor with pillows, this could refer to this type of
sitting/eating arrangement (i.e. "arrange the pillows," cf. NIDOTTE, vol. 3, p. 832).

verses.zh: 主对我如此说：你去设立守望的，使他将所看见的述说。
verses.en: For this is what the Lord[NOTE:1] has told me:“Go, post a guard!He must report what he sees.
notes: The Hebrew term translated “Lord” here and in vv. 8, 16 is אֲדֹנָי (ʾadonay).
verses.commentary:
21:6 Notice the prophet is relaying YHWH's words.

- go, BDB 229, KB 246, Qal IMPERATIVE

- station the lookout, BDB 763, KB 840, Hiphil IMPERATIVE ("sentry,"
lit. "one who watches," BDB 859, KB 1044, Piel PARTICIPLE)

- let him report, BDB 616, KB 665, Hiphil IMPERFECT used in
a JUSSIVE sense

verses.zh: 他看见军队，就是骑马的一对一对地来，又看见驴队，骆驼队，就要侧耳细听。
verses.en: When he sees chariots, teams of horses,[NOTE:1] riders on donkeys,riders on camels,he must be alert,very alert.”
notes: Or “a pair of horsemen.”
verses.commentary:
21:7 He is instructed to watch for a very specific kind of military formation.

- riders on horses in pairs

- a train of donkeys

- a train of camels

The term "riders" (BDB 935) could be understood as chariots pulled by two horses (NKJV, Peshitta;
see SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARIOTS). For #2 and #3, this could
also designate riders (cf. NRSV, LXX). Cavalry were used in places that chariots could not go.

At the sight of this type of military equipment and formation, he is to report immediately
(double use of "attention," BDB 904). Assyria is coming!

verses.zh: 他像狮子吼叫，说：主啊，我白日常站在望楼上，整夜立在我守望所。
verses.en: Then the guard[NOTE:1] cries out:“On the watchtower, O Lord,[NOTE:2] I stand all day long;at my postI am stationed every night.
notes: The Hebrew text has, “the lion,” but this makes little sense here. אַרְיֵה (ʾaryeh, “lion”) probably needs to be emended to an original הָרֹאֶה (haroʾeh, “the one who sees”), i.e., the guard mentioned previously in v. 6. The Dead Sea Scrolls (1Q Isaa) and the Syriac support an original הָרֹאֶה (haroʾeh, “the one who sees”).

The Hebrew term translated “Lord” here is אֲדֹנָי (ʾadonay). Some translations take this to refer to the Lord (cf. NAB, NASB, NRSV), while others take it to refer to the guard’s human master (“my lord”; cf. NIV, NLT).
verses.commentary:
21:8 This is a way of announcing a loud military-type (i.e. like a lion) report by the watchman on
the wall. He has so far seen nothing.

The MT is difficult but the Hebrew manuscripts from DSS make the watchman call out like a lion,
which is the best option for understanding this cryptic Hebrew text.

However, it is possible to see "lion,"
אריה (BDB 71) as a copyist's error for "saw,"
ראה (BDB 906, DSS text has "lookout"), thereby
resulting in the translation, "then the one who sees the sentry" (i.e. watchman) cries out.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LIONS IN THE OT

verses.zh: 看哪，有一队军兵骑着马，一对一对地来。他就说：巴比伦倾倒了！倾倒了！他一切雕刻的神像都打碎于地。
verses.en: Look what’s coming!A charioteer,a team of horses.”[NOTE:1] When questioned, he replies,[NOTE:2] “Babylon has fallen, fallen!All the idols of her gods lie shattered on the ground!”
notes: Or “[with] teams of horses,” or perhaps, “with a pair of horsemen.”
Heb “and he answered and said” (so KJV, ASV).
verses.commentary:
21:9 Suddenly the military formation and equipment come into view! Its presence in Palestine shows
the previous fall of the city of Babylon. This fall is expressed by doubling the VERB
(BDB 656, KB 709, Qal PERFECTS), which is so common in Isaiah. The city
of Babylon fell several times to different Assyrian kings.

Her demise is complete as illustrated by the shattering (BDB 990, KB 1402,
Piel PERFECT) of her idols (cf. Isaiah 46-47). With Babylon defeated
and Elam and Media inactive, Assyria can resume her expansionistic intentions!

verses.zh: 我被打的禾稼，我场上的谷啊，我从万军之耶和华―以色列的　神那里所听见的，都告诉你们了。
verses.en: O my downtrodden people, crushed like stalks on the threshing floor,[NOTE:1] what I have heard from the Lord of Heaven’s Armies,the God of Israel,I have reported to you.
notes: Heb “My trampled one, and the son of the threshing floor.”
verses.commentary:
21:10 The prophet tells the oppressed covenant people that their God (i.e. "Lord
of hosts," "God of Israel") has acted, but how?

- The fall of Babylon was not a victory for them, but a sure promise that Assyria will come.

- The question remains which Babylon is the prophet referring to?

- old Babylon of Merodach-baladan of Isaiah's day (8th century B.C.)

- Neo-Babylon of Nebuchadnezzar II of Ezekiel's and Jeremiah's day (7th century B.C.)

The issue is not one of the reality of the predictive prophecy, but of historical setting!

Just a note about an alternate way of interpreting this verse. It is possible that the ones
who are addressed are the Babylonians who Assyria will destroy. YHWH has earlier heard the fall of Moab
(cf. Isa. 15:5; 16:11) and the prayers of the oppressed Egyptians (cf. Isa. 19:20).

Timeline (Old Testament)

▣ "my afflicted of the threshing floor" This is a Hebrew idiom "son of my threshing floor." The
Hebrew term "son" has many semantic usages in Isaiah.

- son of fatness, Isa. 5:1 (see note at Isa. 5:1)

- son of dawn, Isa. 14:12

- son of the wise, Isa. 19:11

- son of man, Isa. 56:2

- son of a foreign land (lit. "foreigners"), Isa. 56:6

SPECIAL TOPIC: "SONS OF. . ." (OT)

verses.zh: 论度玛的默示：有人声从西珥呼问我说：守望的啊，夜里如何？守望的啊，夜里如何？
verses.en: This is an oracle about Dumah:[NOTE:1] Someone calls to me from Seir,[NOTE:2] “Watchman, what is left of the night?Watchman, what is left of the night?”[NOTE:3]
notes: The noun דּוּמָה (dumah) means “silence,” but here it is a proper name, probably referring to a site in northern Arabia or to the nation of Edom. See BDB 189 s.v. II דּוּמָה. If Dumah was an area in northern Arabia, it would be of interest to the Edomites because of its strategic position on trade routes which they used. See J. N. Oswalt, Isaiah (NICOT), 1:398.
Seir is another name for Edom. See BDB 973 s.v. שֵׂעִיר.
The “night” probably here symbolizes distress and difficult times. See BDB 539 s.v. לַיְלָה.
verses.commentary:
21:11 "The oracle" This (BDB 672) is literally "burden." see full note at Isa. 13:1.

▣

NASB, TEV
"Edom"

NKJV, NRSV, NJB, REB, JPSOA, Peshitta
"Dumah"

LXX
"Idumea"

Rotherham footnote
"silence"

A new message starts (i.e. use of the literary marker, "oracle"; see full note at Isa. 13:1). The
MT has "Dumah" (BDB 189, cf. Gen. 25:14). It is a play on the Hebrew term for "silence" (BDB 189). Edom will be
silenced. Edom was part of the anti-Assyrian coalition, as was Philistia. All were crushed in 711 B.C.
by Sargon II's army.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KINGS OF ASSYRIA

▣ "Seir" This (BDB 973) can refer to the land of Edom (cf. Gen. 32:3; 36:30; Num. 24:18; Deut. 2:4,8,
12,22,29; Jdg. 5:4).

SPECIAL TOPIC: EDOM AND ISRAEL

21:11c-12 This is a very cryptic strophe with several IMPERATIVES. A watchman
on the wall, as in Isa. 21:6 and 8, is addressed by an unknown voice which asks about the time of the night
(twice). The answer is also strange.

- morning comes

- but also night

- ask again

- ask again

It possibly means, "when will all this take place?"

These last two brief oracles of Assyrian attack seem to reflect two groups allied with old Babylon.

verses.zh: 守望的说：早晨将到，黑夜也来。你们若要问就可以问，可以回头再来。
verses.en: The watchman replies,“Morning is coming, but then night.[NOTE:1] If you want to ask, ask;come back again.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Dumah will experience some relief, but it will be short-lived as night returns.

The point of the watchman’s final instructions (“if you want to ask, ask; come again”) is unclear. Perhaps they are included to add realism to the dramatic portrayal. The watchman sends the questioner away with the words, “Feel free to come back and ask again.”

verses.zh: 论阿拉伯的默示：底但结伴的客旅啊，你们必在阿拉伯的树林中住宿。
verses.en: This is an oracle about Arabia:In the thicket of Arabia you spend the night,you Dedanite caravans.
verses.commentary:
21:13 A new message (use of the literary transition marker, "oracle"; see full note at Isa. 13:1) is
addressed to Arabia. It is unsure who the antagonist is.

- Assyria (invasion)

- Kedar (civil war)

It is interesting that "Dumah" (Isa. 21:11) and Seir (Isa. 21:11) are also place names in, or
close to, Arabia.

▣ "the thickets" Isaiah uses "forestry" imagery often. This term (BDB 420) can mean

- forest

- thicket

Since Arabia is desert, the second fits best. It would refer to ravines with thick brushy
vegetation, where animals hide. Now fugitives, refugees, and caravan traders (i.e. Dedanites were a
Bedouin people associated with Sheba) hide there to escape military invasion (cf. Isa. 21:15). They
could not use the usual roads or resting places.

verses.zh: 提玛地的居民拿水来，送给口渴的，拿饼来迎接逃避的。
verses.en: Bring out some water for the thirsty.You who live in the land of Tema,bring some food for the fugitives.
verses.commentary:
21:14 The Arabians are commanded (BDB 87, KB 102, Hiphil IMPERATIVE)
to bring water and food for them.

▣ "Tema" This was a major northern city, home to the worship of the moon goddess.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MOON WORSHIP

verses.zh: 因为他们逃避刀剑和出了鞘的刀，并上了弦的弓与刀兵的重灾。
verses.en: For they flee from the swords—from the drawn sword,and from the battle-ready bow,and from the severity of the battle.

verses.zh: 主对我这样说：「一年之内，照雇工的年数，基达的一切荣耀必归于无有。
verses.en: For this is what the Lord[NOTE:1] has told me: “Within exactly one year[NOTE:2] all the splendor of Kedar will come to an end.
notes: The Hebrew term translated “Lord” here is אֲדֹנָי (ʾadonay).
Heb “in still a year, like the years of a hired worker.” See the note at 16:14.
verses.commentary:
21:16 "In a year, as a hired man would count it" This same idiom of precise timing is found earlier in
Isa. 16:14.

▣ "Kedar" This is another large city of Arabia. It, and by implication all of Arabia's army, will
be defeated. Sargon II attacked this area in 715 B.C.

Again the theological phrase "for the Lord God of Israel has spoken."
It was not the power of ancient armies that directed ANE events, but the God of Israel! This is a claim
to monotheism.

verses.zh: 弓箭手所余剩的，就是基达人的勇士，必然稀少，因为这是耶和华―以色列的　神说的。」
verses.en: Just a handful of archers, the warriors of Kedar, will be left.”[NOTE:1] Indeed,[NOTE:2] the Lord God of Israel has spoken.
notes: Heb “and the remnant of the number of the bow, the mighty men of the sons of Kedar, will be few.”
Or “for” (KJV, ASV, NAB, NASB, NRSV).

READING CYCLE THREE (see
"Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- This chapter lists several nations addressed by YHWH through His prophet, all
introduced by the literary marker, "the oracle about."

- I have mentioned earlier that I think the oracle addressed to the "king of Babylon" really
deals with Assyria (i.e. Isa. 13:1-14:27). This chapter (i.e. Isa. 21:1-10) is about Babylon.

This is not Neo-Babylon of Nabonidus and Nebuchadnezzar (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: KINGS OF NEO-BABYLON), but the Chaldean people close to the
mouth of the Tigris and Euphrates. Their capital would be the city of Babylon and their king
Merodach-baladan, who rebelled in 720 B.C., but was defeated by Sargon II
(see SPECIAL TOPIC: KINGS OF ASSYRIA)
and escaped into the marshes and fled to Elam in 710 B.C. (IVP Bible
Background Commentary, p. 611). The city of Babylon was destroyed by Assyria in 703
B.C. and the King of Assyria took the title "King of Babylon."

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHALDEANS

- This chapter also addresses

- Edom, Isa. 21:11-12

- Arabia, Isa. 21:13-17

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: ISAIAH 21:1-10

1The oracle concerning the wilderness of the sea.

As windstorms in the Negev sweep on,

It comes from the wilderness, from a terrifying land.

2A harsh vision has been shown to me;

The treacherous one still deals treacherously, and the destroyer still destroys.

Go up, Elam, lay siege, Media;

I have made an end of all the groaning she has caused.

3For this reason my loins are full of anguish;

Pains have seized me like the pains of a woman in labor.

I am so bewildered I cannot hear, so terrified I cannot see.

4My mind reels, horror overwhelms me;

The twilight I longed for has been turned for me into trembling.

5They set the table, they spread out the cloth, they eat, they drink;

"Rise up, captains, oil the shields,"

6For thus the Lord says to me,

"Go, station the lookout, let him report what he sees.

7When he sees riders, horsemen in pairs,

A train of donkeys, a train of camels,

Let him pay close attention, very close attention."

8Then the lookout called,

"O Lord, I stand continually by day on the watchtower,

And I am stationed every night at my guard post.

9Now behold, here comes a troop of riders, horsemen in pairs."

And one said, "Fallen, fallen is Babylon;

And all the images of her gods are shattered on the ground."

10O my threshed people, and my afflicted of the threshing floor!

What I have heard from the Lord of hosts,

The God of Israel, I make known to you.
